gap: The search field's placeholder is #BCBCBC — 1.77:1 against the #F7F7F7 paper — while the 21x21px magnifier glyph sitting 35px to its left is #8C8C8C (3.14:1). That is a 48-grey-level split inside one control, and it makes 'Search documents' the palest ink in a pane where every other secondary label (dates, previews, 'Sort by Date', '8 documents · 239 words', 'All changes saved') lands on exactly #8C8C8C. B's placeholder is #999999 against a #989898 icon — matched to within one level.
gapTheirs: B runs two secondary greys and two papers across a single hairline. Sidebar chrome and text — toolbar toggle, folder icon, + button, every date, both preview lines, the sort control, the count, the status line — are #999999 on #FDFDFD paper (2.80:1). The document title 'sea-storm.md' in the same 40px toolbar strip, eight pixels across the divider, is #8C8C8C on #F9F9F9. A puts all of it — pane chrome, dates, previews, status line and editor title — on one grey (#8C8C8C) and one paper (#F7F7F7), 3.14:1, so its library is continuous with its page; B's is a second, paler theme bolted to the side of the first.
verdict: A's library and A's page are the same sheet of paper with a line ruled down it; B's library is a slightly whiter card laid on top, set in a slightly weaker grey, and you feel the seam every time your eye crosses it. B's previews are the ones that cost you: at 2.80:1 the two lines under each filename are texture rather than text, and finding the chapter that starts with the gale means opening files instead of reading the list. B also can't hold a straight left edge — its sort label, file icons and search glyph sit at 14.5, 16.5 and 20 logical px, three edges where A has one — and its row pitch alternates 77/78px instead of A's flat 75. A's one real failure is that its search placeholder is a ghost at 1.8:1 next to its own icon at 3.1:1; that is a bad half-hour for one control, not a pane built on two grey ramps.

states.name: search
states.gap: A does not emphasise the search hit: the matched 'sea' inside the preview stays at #8C8C8C, the exact ink of the words either side of it, so only a pale #B2E7F9 wash marks it — B lifts the matched glyphs to #1C1C1C against a #999999 excerpt, a ~125-level jump you cannot miss. A also gives its Location header no disclosure chevron (B has one after 'Library'), so the folder name is inert text with no visible way to switch or collapse the Location.
states.gapTheirs: B runs every secondary string in the pane at #999999 on a #FDFDFD ground — 2.80:1, under the 3:1 floor: both date stamps, both two-line previews, 'Sort by Date', '2 of 8 documents' and the whole status line. A holds the same strings at #8C8C8C on #F7F7F7 = 3.14:1. Compounding it, B's search magnifier sits at x=20 while its document icons sit at x=16.5 — 3.5px out of the left rail that A aligns exactly (both at 16.5).
states.verdict: B builds a better search row and a better door — the matched word goes black inside the wash, and the chevron says the Location can be changed — but it then greys out everything you actually scan: dates, previews, count and status line all sit at 2.80:1 and go soft the moment you stop staring. A keeps the same content one step darker and lines the search field up with the document icons under it to the pixel, which is the difference between a column you read and one you squint at. Neither highlights 'sea' in 'sea-storm', so the top result in both shows no visible reason for being there — a search list that cannot mark a filename match is not finished. A wins on legibility, and only just; fix A's match emphasis and add the header chevron and it stops being close.

Row separators geometrically identical in both: 1px, inset 46px left / 14px right.
Selected-row tint delta identical: A #F2F2F2 on #F7F7F7, B #F8F8F8 on #FDFDFD — 5 levels each. Both are near-invisible; the 4px blue bar is doing all the work.
Row height A 74px vs B 78px logical; B is 4px airier per row.
Right rail is clean in both — count, dates and status all flush at x=705 device. B's '+' button sits at 708, 1.5px proud of that rail.
Neither pane offers a clear (×) control in the search field once a query is entered.

Editor side (not this piece, noted only): A hangs the '#' 26.5px into the margin so heading and body share a left edge; B sets '#' on the body edge and pushes 'The storm' 26px right, breaking the left margin.
Both clip the status line at the viewport bottom — 26px of bar for text that needs more.
